edits: quote_status: paraphrase-only **Located operations:** the torus cell presentation (p. 5); the product fundamental group (p. 34); path lifting (pp. 60–61); integer-translation and Klein-bottle quotient actions (p. 74). The sphere comparison is located at Proposition 1.14, p. 35. These are selected passages, not a complete surface-classification survey. ### Consulted digital version The corrected PDF linked from the author's Cornell page, `https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf`, consulted September 29, 2026. The reference is the 2002 book in its author-maintained online version; no collation to an original print impression is asserted. Printed page numbers are followed below by one-based PDF pages. Text and diagrams were inspected together. The passages are paraphrase-only; no quotation has been promoted. ## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p001` — Torus cell presentation and independent generators Opposite sides of a square are identified in pairs, yielding one vertex, two edges and one face. The product rule gives the torus fundamental group as two independent integer windings. - **Locator:** “Cell Complexes,” p. 5 (PDF 14); Proposition 1.12 and Example 1.13, p. 34 (PDF 43). - **Status:** paraphrase-only. - **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, text and screenshot inspection; no OCR. - **Source relation:** extracted. - **Evidential action:** supports. - **Consumers:** [[symbolon/episteme/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]]. - **Use boundary:** four polygon sides before identification are not four quotient vertices. ## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p002` — Chosen lifts and closed loops A path lifts uniquely after a starting lift is chosen. Which loops lift to loops depends on the covering subgroup. A homotopy class retains less information than a parametrised path. - **Locator:** Proposition 1.30 and ensuing path-lifting discussion, p. 60 (PDF 69); Propositions 1.31–1.32, p. 61 (PDF 70). - **Status:** paraphrase-only. - **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, text and screenshot inspection; no OCR. - **Source relation:** extracted; the worked torus endpoint comparison is developed in the consumer. - **Evidential action:** qualifies. - **Consumers:** [[symbolon/episteme/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]]. - **Use boundary:** an endpoint displacement does not reconstruct every turn or timing of a travelled path. ## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p003` — Different quotient groups, different covers Integer translations of the plane give a torus quotient. The Klein-bottle action includes a glide-reflection; its index-two translation subgroup gives a torus double cover. These are different covering maps. - **Locator:** Example 1.42, p. 74 (PDF 83); compare Example 1.46, p. 77 (PDF 86). - **Status:** paraphrase-only. - **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, diagrams and text inspected together; no OCR. - **Source relation:** extracted. - **Evidential action:** supports and distinguishes. - **Consumers:** [[symbolon/episteme/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]]. - **Use boundary:** the plane-to-torus map has infinite fibres; the torus-to-Klein-bottle map has two-point fibres. ## Passage card — `hatcher-2002-algebraic-topology-p004` — The sphere comparison For spheres of dimension at least two, the fundamental group is trivial. Thus a sphere has no non-contractible loop class; this does not prohibit paths or physical motion on it. - **Locator:** Proposition 1.14 and its proof, p. 35 (PDF 44). - **Status:** paraphrase-only. - **Verification:** assistant, 2026-09-29; author-hosted corrected PDF, text and screenshot inspection; no OCR. - **Source relation:** extracted; the distinction from physical motion states the consumer's scope. - **Evidential action:** qualifies. - **Consumers:** [[symbolon/episteme/arguments/A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos|Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos]]. - **Use boundary:** no physical conservation or optimality theorem follows from simply connectedness.
